key_insight: A fair, unified evaluation shows that only the newest Prior-data Fitted Network-based graph foundation models beat well-tuned GNN baselines for node property prediction.
engineering_relevance: For real-world graph systems, the result suggests careful benchmark design matters more than model branding, and that accuracy gains may come with higher inference latency.
method: Re-evaluated 9 recent graph foundation models on node property prediction.
Compared all models under a fair, rigorous setting against strong GNN baselines.
Focused on predictive performance and inference cost trade-offs.
evidence_signal: The paper reports a reevaluation of 9 GFMs and finds only the most recent Prior-data Fitted Networks outperform well-tuned GNNs, but at higher inference cost.
watch_item: Cross-paper comparisons can be misleading because evaluation protocols differ widely; deployment should also account for the added inference cost of the best-performing GFMs.
paper_title: A Fair Evaluation of Graph Foundation Models for Node Property Prediction
